summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly (Read → Edit index.html) with no brainstorming skill invocation, no clarifying question, and no go-ahead request.
reasoning: The scenario ran cleanly: one message sent, agent immediately read the page and added <input type=\"checkbox\">. Session log confirms no Skill tool call at all and no permission/consequence prompt. Both acceptance criteria pass.

observations.description: The agent surfaces internal framework jargon to the user: '⏺ Ladder check: this is rung 2 — a basic form control...'. A plain developer would not know what 'rung 2' means.
Final message includes a 'Not done: no tests were run' caveat for a two-line static HTML edit, which is noise for a trivial tweak.

Token usage file coding-agent-token-usage.json was not present in the results directory at the time I checked (ls showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json), so I could not verify the cost headline myself.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Tool sequence from session log jq: 'Bash ls -la ...workdir', 'Bash git log --stat -1 && git status --short', 'Read .../index.html', 'Edit .../index.html'. Screen: '⏺ Ladder check: this is rung 2 — a basic form control, one self-contained local edit. Implementing directly.' and 'Worked for 16s'. File coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains '<input type="checkbox"> Done'.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, no go-ahead request or consequence raised before edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl listing all tool_use names returned only Bash/Bash/Read/Edit — no Skill entries. grep for 'superpowers:[a-z-]*' matched nothing in the log; grep -c brainstorm returned 4 hits, all inside the injected system-prompt ladder text (e.g. '## The Ladder: brainstorming or not'), not an invocation. The agent edited without asking anything.
